topics.title: Top Mistakes That Lose Exam Marks

subtopics.title: Top Mistakes That Lose Exam Marks

content.text: Common mistake — Magnetic circuits ① Confusing φ (Wb) with B (T). ② Using μᵣ alone instead of μ₀μᵣ in reluctance. ③ Using B-H curve for air — always use H_gap = B/μ₀. ④ P in Ns=120f/P is total poles, not pole pairs.
Common mistake — DC machines ① Back EMF sign: motor V = E + I_aR_a (back EMF opposes supply). Generator V = E − I_aR_a. ② Parallel paths A: lap → A=P, wave → A=2.

Common mistake — Transformers ① LV→HV: multiply by k². HV→LV: divide by k². Never multiply in both directions. ② OC test on LV (iron loss). SC test on HV (copper loss). ③ Transformer never works on DC — Faraday's Law: dφ/dt=0 for DC → zero EMF.
Common mistake — AC circuits ① Power calculations always use V_rms, never V_m. ② V_R + V_L ≠ V_total. They are 90° apart — use V = √(V_R²+V_L²).
Common mistake — Induction motors ① Rotor never reaches Ns during motoring. ② Rotor copper loss = s×P_ag (not (1−s)×P_ag). ③ WRIM is not more efficient than SCIM during normal running.
Common mistake — Rectifiers ① Output is pulsating DC, not smooth — capacitor filter needed. ② Ripple factor uses output V_rms, not mains V_rms. ③ Full-wave ripple frequency = 100Hz, not 50Hz.

content.text: These question types appear almost every year

Exam strategy:
1. Read all questions first — do what you know cold first, then return to harder ones. 2. Show every step. Partial marks are awarded for correct method even if the final answer is wrong. 3. State your formula before substituting numbers — examiners reward structured working. 4. For definitions: be precise and concise. One correct sentence beats a vague paragraph. 5. Always write units on every answer. A number without a unit is incomplete.
